title: SSL certificates
desc: Automatically issue and renew certificates via ACME, or upload / read local certificate files
renewOffDesc: ACME certificates will not be renewed automatically before they expire. You can renew them manually from each card.
empty: No certificates yet. Request or upload one, or import a Lucky config in "Settings → Backup & Migration"
confirmDelete: Delete this certificate? Mapped files are kept
remarkPlaceholder: Used as the file name when mapping is enabled, e.g. nas.example.com
domainsPlaceholder: One per line; wildcards such as *.example.com and public IP addresses are supported
emailPlaceholder: Leave empty to use the default email from renewal settings
secretPlaceholder: A saved secret is shown as ********
zonePlaceholder: Leave empty to look up the zone of the validation record in DNS; a subdomain hosted at another provider is detected automatically, or fill it in, e.g. web.example.com
disableAuthCheck: Query only the DNS servers above, not the authoritative servers
skipCheck: Skip the check (validate directly after waiting 20 seconds)
keyPemPlaceholder: A saved private key is shown as ********; leave unchanged to keep the current value
fileHelp: Files are checked periodically and reloaded automatically; suited to certificates maintained by other tools such as certbot.
postScriptPlaceholder: e.g. docker exec nginx nginx -s reload
envHelp: Environment variables: certName certDir certFile keyFile
deployHelp: After a certificate is issued, renewed or updated, copy it to local directories, push it to other hosts, or restart the containers that use it. You can add several targets. Failures are retried hourly and send a "Certificate: deployment failed" notification
deployConnectionPlaceholder: Pick an SSH connection from Web Terminal
deployNoConnections: No SSH connections yet; add one in Web Terminal first
deployUntrustedHelp: Automatic deployment never trusts an unknown host. Connect to this host once in Web Terminal to record its host key
deployFileNamesHelp: File names for the certificate (full chain) and the private key. Fill in both to write only these two files. Leave empty to use the certificate mapping names (remark.crt / .pem / .key), which requires a remark
deployCommandHelp: Runs on the remote host with {'$'}certName {'$'}certDir {'$'}certFile {'$'}keyFile available
deployLocalCommandHelp: Runs on this machine with {'$'}certName {'$'}certDir {'$'}certFile {'$'}keyFile available. When Gately runs in Docker, the directory and command are inside the container
deployContainersHelp: These containers are restarted in turn after the certificate changes; useful when they mount the mapping directory
deployContainersError: Could not list containers ({error}); you can type container names directly
savedAcme: Saved; issuance runs in the background when needed
renewStarted: Issuance started; see the log for progress
httpTip: The CA connects to port 80 of each domain from the public internet. Wildcard domains are not supported. If a Web Service listens on port 80, it answers the validation automatically; otherwise Gately temporarily listens on the port below.
httpPortHelp: 0 means 80. Use this when your router forwards public port 80 to another local port.
profileDefault: Default (chosen by the CA, usually 90 days)
profileHelp: The ACME profile; you can also type another profile name the CA supports
networkHelp: Network used to reach the CA and DNS provider and to check TXT propagation during issuance. Choose IPv4 only when the host has an IPv6 address but IPv6 does not work
profileShortLivedHelp: Valid for about 6 days and renewed automatically {hours} hours before expiry; Let's Encrypt issues IP address certificates only with this profile
ipCertTip: IP address certificates need the Let's Encrypt short-lived profile and HTTP-01 validation (the CA connects to port 80 of the IP)
ipCertTipCustom: IP address certificates need HTTP-01 validation (the CA connects to port 80 of the IP)
